bounded_statement: The report's selected result (Welch's two-sample t-test, t = 11.079, df = 42.554, p < 0.0001, samples of 24 per aspect) is obtained by entering all 48 stake-day rows into a procedure that treats every row as an independent observation, even though the data description states the independent unit is stake_id and only 8 stakes (4 per aspect) exist, with each stake contributing 6 repeated daily readings. The reported degrees of freedom, sample sizes, and p-value are therefore not supported at the stated independent-unit level; this review makes no claim about whether a correctly unit-aggregated analysis would or would not reach significance, nor about the direction or physical plausibility of the aspect effect.

counterevidence_considered.description: Slope aspect is fixed at the stake level (a between-unit factor), and the per-stake mean melt values separate cleanly by aspect (north stake means about 9, 11, 13, 15 mm versus south stake means about 17.5, 20.5, 22.5, 25.5 mm), so the direction and existence of an aspect difference are not artifacts of the pooling; only the reported n, df, and p-value are inflated. The report also labels the observations transparently as 'stake-day readings' rather than concealing the repeated structure.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: Non-overlapping per-stake means between aspects; between-stake factor design

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to find any point in the workflow or report where the repeated stake-day rows are collapsed to one value per independent unit or where the within-stake dependence is otherwise modelled: I checked load_readings, split_by_aspect, welch_dof, and main in workflow/analysis.py for grouping by the 'stake' key it stores, per-stake averaging, mixed/random-effects structure, or cluster-robust adjustment, and found none — the 'stake' field is loaded but never used in the analysis. I also checked whether the data description might permit treating rows as independent (e.g., re-randomised units), but it explicitly states the same eight stakes were revisited each morning and nothing was re-randomised, and it names stake_id as the independent-unit column. Finally, I verified the reported df of 42.554 is only consistent with 24 observations per group, not with 4 stakes per group. The issue could not be falsified.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py buckets every row's melt value by aspect (split_by_aspect) and passes all 24 repeated readings per group directly to scipy.stats.ttest_ind, with no aggregation to per-stake means and no modelling of the stake-level clustering, so the six repeated measurements of each authorized independent unit (stake_id) are each entered as separate observations into a row-independent two-sample test, inflating the effective sample size from 4 per group to 24 per group.
